lens: Enterprise LMS (Lessonly/Seismic): curricula, assignments, certifications, manager-assigned drills
name: Call Cockpit Curriculum
one_liner: A dark live cockpit plus a curriculum-first library: ordered paths, a browsable persona catalog, and an AI wizard, built on shadcn/ui with OpenAI models wired into voice, coaching and grading.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the Enterprise LMS lens: ordered paths (curricula), manager-assigned drills with due dates, certification gates, and a team view. Research changed two things. Second Nature and Hyperbound both lead with persona libraries and scorecards, so the library becomes the front door, not a three-item dropdown. Grain's 1-5 criterion dots with timestamped evidence show how live scoring can stay legible. Expected scores: A look 8, B UX 7, C unique 6, D live coaching 5.5 (only if cue latency holds), E library and wizard 6. Business: F1 SaaS 6, F2 entities 8, F3 (10 = not worth building) 3.

design_language.typography: Geist Sans for UI and headings (600-700 weight, -0.02em tracking on display sizes). Geist Mono for timers, scores and transcript timestamps. 16px minimum body on mobile. Inter and Sora are removed.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Radius 14px for cards, 10px for controls, full pill for chips. 1px hairline borders plus one soft shadow. The blurred gradient orb is replaced by a 2D waveform ring driven by mic level; the three.js orb survives only on the landing hero.
design_language.motion: Motion springs (stiffness 320, damping 30) for rubric meters. Cue chips slide in over 180ms. A criterion that changes flashes once. Everything is gated by prefers-reduced-motion.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.75 stroke. A custom five-dot rating glyph for 1-5 criteria. Persona avatars are generated monograms tinted by role, never stock photos.
design_language.theme_modes: Light by default for library, progress and team. Dark night mode for the live cockpit and landing hero. Follows prefers-color-scheme with a visible toggle; both modes are designed, not inverted.

navigation_and_ia: Desktop: a slim left rail with Learn (assigned paths and next drill), Library, Practice, Progress and Team (Team only on org accounts), plus a persistent New persona button. Mobile: a bottom tab bar with Learn, Library, a centre Call button, Progress and Me. Cmd-K is global. The Trainer dropdown is replaced by Paths (ordered curricula) and Library (browse), so "pick a scenario" becomes "pick a path or persona". Existing routes redirect: /trainer/scenarios opens Library, and /dashboard becomes Progress.

live_coaching_and_scoring: A coach runs as a second, cheaper model stream fed by the same transcript, never by the persona prompt, so realism holds. Each rep turn yields three things: rubric deltas for the five criteria, each with a quote and a one-line reason; at most one cue, chosen by priority (objection alert, then missed discovery, then the next talk-track step); and a next-best question. Cues are rate-limited to one per 25 seconds and expire after 12 seconds. Silent mode turns them off. Live scores are labelled live estimate until the final GPT grader runs with the existing evidence rule; the debrief shows where the two disagreed. If the model call fails, the existing keyword heuristic is the fallback. Text mode gets cues first because its latency is lower.
persona_library_and_wizard: Ship a persona pack format: one folder per pack holding personas, scenarios, rubrics and a short validation script, all in the repo. Target about 150 personas at launch across roughly 20 industries and the sales roles in the brief, each tagged by role, industry, difficulty and objection type. CI validates every pack with a zod schema and a dry-run against a mock persona, so contributors can open PRs safely. The wizard is source-first: a job description, product URL, CRM notes, an ICP form or a pasted call. It drafts a persona and rubric with sourced fields, runs a dry run, and saves privately or opens a pack PR. Private packs stay local; authors are credited on every shared pack.
signature_moments: A violet cue chip appears under the rep's last sentence and names the exact next question.
Five-dot criterion ratings move and flash once per turn, then settle under a live estimate label.
Replay this moment turns one weak line in the debrief into a 90-second drill.
The pack gallery shows author, pack version and usage count on each card, so contributors get visible credit.
A three-way coach mode switch (Silent, Whisper, Tough buyer) sits on the pre-call card and in the cockpit.
openai_fund_angle: Concrete showcase, not a logo. (1) The OpenAI Realtime API is a selectable voice engine next to ElevenLabs, and the cockpit footer shows which engine and model are live. (2) GPT-4.1-mini (the existing default) grades and drives the wizard, and a smaller GPT model produces the live cues; the landing hero and README show a Built with OpenAI models row. (3) Codex is the contributor engine: the repo ships an AGENTS.md and a persona-pack scaffold, so contributors use Codex CLI to generate and validate packs, and Codex reviews pack PRs in CI. Invitations: good-first-pack issues and a credited pack gallery. Avoid OpenAI brand colours or logos beyond the permitted badge.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0: CSS-variable tokens, Geist fonts, shadcn primitives, keep Tailwind 3. Phase 1: new shell (rail, mobile tab bar, Cmd-K) and Library seeded with the three existing scenarios as the first pack; redirect old routes. Phase 2: pack format, CI validation, grow toward 150 personas. Phase 3: live cockpit with the coach stream and live rubric, behind a flag, keeping the current chat as fallback. Phase 4: the wizard. Phase 5: Progress, Paths and the Team view, which needs org data.

risks: Cue latency: a cue arriving 2-3 seconds late lands after the rep has moved on. Mitigate with a fast model, rate limits and expiry.
Crowded market: Second Nature, Hyperbound, PitchMonster, Kendo and Yoodli already exist. The OSS core must differentiate on self-hosting, open packs and bring-your-own model, not feature parity.
Persona quality varies across contributors. Pack CI, dry runs and a verified tag are needed before the library claims scale.
Scope is XL: nine screens plus the wizard and cockpit. Ship the Team view as a read-only MVP first.
Tailwind 3 is kept on purpose; moving to Tailwind 4 during the redesign would double the risk.
A public demo with live voice needs quotas or text-only mode so that keys and costs stay controlled.
Brand risk: the OpenAI badge must follow its usage guidelines, and the README must not imply endorsement.
